summary.headline: Gala Precision Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to about ₹90 crore with net profit up 46% to ₹11 crore; order book grew 44% YoY past ₹100 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of about ₹90 crore (up 21% YoY), EBITDA of about ₹16 crore (up 45%, margin 16.76%, up 135 bps) and net profit of about ₹11 crore (up 46%, margin 11.81%). Order book grew 44% YoY to cross ₹100 crore in a single quarter. Management reiterated 25% growth for FY27 and guided EBITDA margin of 17-19%. Transcript quality is poor in places, so some figures (segment splits, Chennai revenue comparisons, capacity numbers) are as best interpreted from the call.

financial_highlights.value: crossed ₹100 crore in a single quarter

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue held back from Q1 delivered in Q2

financial_highlights.value: DSS about 50%, SFS about 31%, CSS about 16% (as stated; DSS and SFS split unclear in transcript)
Renewable energy about 42%; industrial, mobility and consumer rest
₹58 crore (₹15 crore fund-based WC, ₹10 crore non-fund WC, ₹28 crore term loan)

segments.name: DSS (as referred to on call)
segments.commentary: Largest segment; management said DSS and SFS drive growth, with both developing domestic and global markets. Utilisation said to be highest of the segments, around 80-85% (as stated).

segments.name: SFS (spring/fastener-type products, as referred to on call)
segments.commentary: About 31% of H1 revenue; growth driver with DSS. Chennai SFS revenue ramped from about ₹0.64 crore in H1 FY26 (started Aug 2025) to about ₹22 crore in Q2 and about ₹62 crore in H1 FY27 per the analyst's reconciliation, which management did not fully dispute.

segments.name: CSS (as referred to on call)
segments.commentary: About 16% of H1 revenue; mainly India-focused and growing slower than DSS and SFS.

segments.name: Renewable energy end-market
segments.commentary: About 42% of H1 revenue. Wind demand softer in H1 per management, but share of wallet with wind OEMs is 5-25-30%; new onshore/offshore wind and tower products added.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of about 25%, reiterated despite Q1 dispatch holdback.
Chennai phase 2 (about ₹50 crore annual capacity) expected operational by Jan 2027 (Q4 FY27), with possible partial sales in Nov-Dec 2026; phase 1 (about ₹60 crore/yr) running near full.
Planned capex of about ₹45 crore in FY28; new facility/land at Vara (about 10 acres bought earlier) to add DSS and SFS capacity in FY28.
Electrolyzer order expected to bring about ₹2 crore revenue in FY27; ₹40-50 crore potential over next 2-3 years from electrolyzer and safety applications.
Management expects renewable energy share of 35-38%, industrial 35-37%, mobility about 25% over the next 2-3 years; spring and SFS together about 42% of turnover in 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Chennai (SFS) phase 1 capacity about ₹60 crore/yr, running near full; phase 2 about ₹50 crore/yr targeted for Q4 FY27 after shifting machines into a 10,000 sq ft area.
Vara plant: plan to double capacity to about 450 kg-equivalent via new lines and line balancing; in phases; MoU for a Vara-adjacent parcel signed June 19 with legal process delayed.
Installed annual capacity cited at about 450 (unit not clear) across Vara and Chennai; utilisation about 80-85% overall, CSS lowest and DSS highest (as stated).
Nandesh (Maharashtra) 1.2 MW AC solar plant commissioned Oct 30, 2026; capex about ₹6.2 crore; expected annual saving about ₹1.35 crore; payback about 4.5 years.
Backup plan: long-lease premises shortlisted if government land approvals are delayed; Chennai/Sinai capacity to be extended for FY29 by acquiring a 3-5 acre parcel.
Chennai SFS plant is the new capacity mentioned as 'Sinai' in the transcript (new fastener and spring facility with installed capacity cited as 4,006 MT; capacity figure may be mis-transcribed).
demand_pricing: Order book up 44% YoY and crossed ₹100 crore in a single quarter, across key end-user industries.
Growth from three pillars, each about 10%: organic growth, new components from existing customers, and new customers (about 30% total growth cited).
Wind: India wind market growth slowed in H1, but company share of wallet with wind OEMs is 5-30%; onshore sales continue and offshore wind parts started exporting this quarter.
Europe: new automotive Tier-1 approvals in India; pilot supplies for European customers in Q3 and Q4 FY27; added sales staff in Europe and US.
Competitive intensity in export markets not seen as changing materially, per management.
Aerospace and gas turbine: exotic material (Inconel, stainless) capability demonstrated in springs; management sees about 25% growth potential in these segments over 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q2 revenue is from the order held back in Q1, and is growth volume or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹3 crore of held-back Q1 dispatches were included in Q2; growth is mainly volume, from organic growth, new components from existing customers and new customers, each about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Chennai phase 2 still on track and how will capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 targeted for Q4 FY27; FY28 capex plan of ₹40-45 crore unchanged. Capex is funded by internal accruals and general corporate funds; banks do not fund land purchases, and more term loans may be needed in FY28 depending on fund flow.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin improve in FY27 after falling from 19.16% in FY24 to 16.51% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a richer product mix and lower manpower and other expenses (manpower cost down, as stated), with last year's product losses no longer present.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential and timing from electrolyzer customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Electrolyzer order received in June 2026 expected to give about ₹2 crore of sales in FY27; discussions with other electrolyzer companies in India and globally could add ₹40-50 crore over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was operating cash flow weak in H1 despite profit, and what is the working capital plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed weak H1 cash flow to export-heavy sales and higher inventory; a KPMG-type working capital diagnosis is complete, with implementation targeted early FY28 and benefits taking one to two years (as stated).

qa_highlights.question: Is Chennai's revenue contribution explaining H1 growth, and what is the Vara underlying growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not dispute the analyst's reconciliation that most H1 growth came from Chennai SFS, which started ramping after Aug 2025; Vara growth underlying was close to about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Is management maintaining the 17-19% EBITDA margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said 17-19% EBITDA margin target remains unchanged.

risks_watch: Dependence on government land approvals and delays in Vara land MoU; backup long-lease plan not yet finalised.

Working-capital intensity: H1 operating cash flow weak versus reported profit; inventory days reported differently (around 100 per management), and working-capital optimisation benefits only from FY28.
Chennai phase 2 timing (Q4 FY27) and capacity ramp-up; utilisation of CSS and DSS lower than DSS/SFS.
Wind segment slowdown in India in H1; growth depends on new wind product categories and offshore wind ramp.
Europe and US export growth depends on new customer wins and newly added sales staff; ~36% of revenue is export.
Capacity constraint at Chennai in FY29 with land acquisition still pending.
Transcript is of poor quality in parts; key figures (segment split, capacity units, inventory days) should be verified against the company's filing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and order book growth and reiterated FY27 targets, but cautious and somewhat evasive on working capital, inventory days and land acquisition timing, which management tied to government approvals and legal delays.
key_quotes: Order will grew by 44% year on year, crossing 100 crore for the first time in a single quarter, reflecting a healthy demand across all key end user industries.
So I think for this electrolyzer order which we received in June this year we are looking at approximate sales of two-prone routines in this financial year.
And we are on track to grow 25% sales in this year as well.

adds.what: Chennai SFS phase 2 about ₹50 crore/yr capacity (after shifting machines into 10,000 sq ft area)
Nandesh (Maharashtra) 1.2 MW AC solar plant (energy, not productive capacity)
Vara plant expansion to about 450 kg-equivalent via new lines and line balancing, in phases; planned FY28 capex about ₹45 crore

growth.why: Management reiterated about 25% FY27 revenue growth and 17-19% EBITDA margin, backed by an order book up 44% YoY past ₹100 crore, Chennai phase 2 (~₹50 crore/yr) due by January 2027, and planned ~₹45 crore FY28 capex at Vara; utilisation ~80-85% and transcript quality is poor, so capacity figures are uncertain.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin 16.76% in Q2 (up 135 bps YoY) and management held the 17-19% FY27 target, citing richer product mix, lower manpower cost and no repeat of last year's product losses.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Chennai SFS phase 2 (about ₹50 crore/yr) is under construction with a firm January 2027 operational date, after phase 1 (about ₹60 crore/yr) already ran near full.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book up 44% YoY past ₹100 crore and management reiterated about 25% FY27 revenue growth, with growth of about 10% each from organic, existing-customer new components and new customers.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 80-85% with DSS highest, and a ₹40-45 crore FY28 capex plan at Vara (about 450 kg-equivalent) is already set, with the MoU for an adjacent parcel signed June 19 but legal process delayed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only reiterated the 25% FY27 growth and 17-19% margin targets despite the Q1 holdback of about ₹3 crore, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Weak H1 operating cash flow versus profit, Vara land approvals still pending, and Chennai phase 2 timing (Q4 FY27) could slip the 25% growth target.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Electrolyzer order received June 2026 is expected to bring about ₹2 crore of FY27 revenue, and pilot supplies to European customers run in Q3-Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Working capital diagnosis implementation
rows.why: KPMG-type working capital diagnosis is complete, with benefits taking 1-2 years, and H1 operating cash flow was weak against profit due to export-heavy sales and higher inventory (inventory days cited around 100).

rows.label: Europe Tier-1 auto and offshore wind exports
rows.why: New automotive Tier-1 approvals in India, pilot supplies to European customers in Q3-Q4 FY27, and offshore wind parts began exporting this quarter; export share is about 36% of H1 revenue.

rows.label: Funding the FY28 capex
rows.why: Capex of ₹40-45 crore is funded by internal accruals and general funds, and more term loans may be needed in FY28 depending on fund flow, against ₹58 crore bank sanctions already in place.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book, the 25% FY27 growth target and the 17-19% margin, but cautious on working capital, inventory days and Vara land timing; analysts pressed on Chennai's share of H1 growth and cash conversion.
